note: An empty map: the size announces the count octet and nothing else (size 1). The boundary the malformed sizes below are adjacent to.
One pair: count 2 (even), size 3 = the count octet and the two item octets. The smallest map the parity rule admits.

An empty list, sized like the empty map: the count octet is the whole content. Legal but *not* canonical — the narrowest encoding of an empty list is list0 (0x45) — so this vector does not claim the octets are the canonical form, which is the distinction the two vectors together pin.
An empty array: the size counts the count octet and the element constructor, so two octets with no element data. Same accounting as the artifact's ten-null example, one step down at the empty case.
Two zero-width elements: the count says two, the constructor says null, and the element data is empty because null carries no payload.
One fixed-width element: the element data is exactly the one octet the declared constructor carries. The boundary the short and long element data below crosses.
null carries no payload at all, so one octet is the whole encoding. The boundary the trailing-octet negatives are adjacent to.
true carries no payload at all, so one octet is the whole encoding. The boundary the trailing-octet negatives are adjacent to.
false carries no payload at all, so one octet is the whole encoding. The boundary the trailing-octet negatives are adjacent to.
uint0 carries no payload at all, so one octet is the whole encoding. The boundary the trailing-octet negatives are adjacent to.
ulong0 carries no payload at all, so one octet is the whole encoding. The boundary the trailing-octet negatives are adjacent to.
list0 carries no payload at all, so one octet is the whole encoding. The boundary the trailing-octet negatives are adjacent to.
A fixed-width encoding with exactly the one octet it declares.

Two pairs with keys that differ, which is the same octet shape as the duplicate negatives with one payload octet changed. The control that keeps a refusal of those from being read as enforcement of the rule.
